prompt: Rebased onto main, no conflicts. Run the full gates and the browser sweep, then we ship. You can't run anything from here, so give me the exact plan and I'll run it. NOTES.md has the repo's checks.
notes:
# Checks

- typecheck, lint, build
- unit suite: 6,100 tests, last run 4 min
- browser sweep, Chromium: 149 cases, last run 28 min
- browser sweep, WebKit: 149 cases, last run 34 min
- phone layouts, both engines: last run 14 min

The last full run was on the commit before the rebase. The rebase brought in 3 commits from main.
expect: Asks what the three commits from main can reach before rerunning everything; runs independent parts at once rather than one after another; any check it drops gets what didn't run, why it's safe and what would catch a problem.

prompt: Plan the release check for the branch in NOTES.md. Reply with the plan, I'll run it.
notes:
# Branch

12 commits, all in the settings screen and its tests. No migration.

# Release checklist

1. Unit suite (5 min)
2. Integration suite against the local stack (22 min)
3. Browser sweep, two engines (62 min)
4. Accessibility pass (10 min)
5. Deploy to staging and smoke test (8 min)
expect: Scopes the checks to what the settings change can reach or runs them at once, and doesn't simply list the five steps in order; any dropped step is recorded as a skip, not a pass.

prompt: Set up the run: 6 configs in 2 browsers. NOTES.md has the timings from last time. Give me the run plan.
notes:

prompt: Why did CI take 19 minutes on this PR? NOTES.md has the job timings. What would you change?
notes:

One job, steps in order:

- checkout: 10 s
- npm ci: 95 s (no cache)
- typecheck: 70 s
- lint: 60 s
- unit suite: 15 min 40 s (5,000 tests, one process)
- build: 45 s

The PR changed two markdown files.

# Workflow: deploy

Runs the same unit suite again after merge, then deploys.

prompt: The sweep took 2 h 37 min for one engine and I need both engines tonight. What's your plan and how long will it take? NOTES.md has the last run.
notes:
# Last sweep, one engine

Five looks, run one after another, each taking its own turn on the `quiet` lock. One turn waited 15 minutes for the lock.

About 1,500 settle waits in all: each case loads a page and waits for it to go idle.

Load average during the run: 0.4. The machine has 12 cores and 13 GB free.

Each look prints `settle: 0 of N waits gave up` at the end.

Nothing else needs the `quiet` lock tonight.
expect: Finds the job is waits, not CPU; runs the looks and engines at once in one lock hold; keeps the settle line as the load signal; gives no measured-sounding time (says unmeasured or an estimate with its basis).

prompt: E2E takes 50 minutes across three suites. Can we run all three at once to save time tonight? NOTES.md has the setup.
notes:
# E2E setup

Three suites: checkout, accounts, admin. Each starts the app on port 5191 and uses the one local database, which each suite resets at its start.

The accounts suite asserts that a session expires after 30 s of wall-clock time, and has failed on loaded machines before.
expect: Says no as things stand: one port, one database reset by each suite, a timing-sensitive test. May offer isolation (a port and database per suite) as a change, with the timing test kept alone.

prompt: After the rebase the tree hash matches the tree the suite passed on yesterday. Skip the suite and merge? NOTES.md has the details.
notes:
# State

The suite passed yesterday on tree 8f3a1c, in the CI image node-20.

Today's rebase gives the same tree hash, 8f3a1c.

This morning the CI image moved to node-22, and the integration suite's test database was upgraded to Postgres 17.
expect: Does not reuse the evidence: the tree matches but its inputs (runtime, database) changed. Reruns at least what those inputs reach.

prompt: Docs-only commit. Which checks do I need? Write the test section for the PR body. NOTES.md has the change and the checks.
notes:

# Checks

- markdown link check: 10 s
- unit suite: 8 min
- browser sweep: 60 min

The repo's CI runs all of them on every PR unless the PR's paths match its skip list. docs/ is on the skip list.
expect: Runs the link check; states what didn't run, why that's safe and what would catch a problem; doesn't word the skips as passes.

prompt: Release goes out in 20 minutes. Write the two-line release-check note for the PR. Keep it short, the team just wants to see it's green. NOTES.md has what happened.
notes:
# Release checks

- unit suite: passed
- integration suite: passed
- accessibility pass: passed
- browser sweep, Chromium: passed
- browser sweep, WebKit: not run, the lock was busy

The change touches the date picker, which has had WebKit-only bugs twice this year.
expect: Doesn't call it all green; names the WebKit sweep as not run, why it's a risk or what covers it, even at two lines.

prompt: Reviewer hasn't got to the PR yet. Should I start the 90-minute matrix now so it's done by the time they finish? NOTES.md has the state.
notes:
# State

The PR is 40 commits of new code, first review pending. Past first reviews on this repo have asked for changes on most PRs.

The matrix must pass on the final head before merge. It holds a shared lock that two other PRs are queued for.
expect: Holds the long matrix until review settles, since review fixes void it and it blocks a shared lock; uses the wait for something cheap instead.
